_description: AgriSmart AI Agronomic Knowledge Base Schema for Crop Disease Diagnosis

symptoms: Concentric dark brown circular lesions with target-board appearance on older leaves
Narrow chlorotic yellow halo surrounding necrotic margins
Progressive lower-to-upper canopy progression via rain splash transmission

treatment.organic: Foliar application of Copper Hydroxide (2g/L) or Trichoderma viride biological bio-fungicide.
treatment.conventional: Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L) or Azoxystrobin 23% SC (1ml/L) foliar spray.
treatment.dosage: 500 liters spray volume per acre with hollow cone nozzle at 2.5 bar.
treatment.timing: Early morning or late afternoon during clear, dry weather when leaves are dry.

precautions: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; surface leaf moisture promotes fungal spore germination.
Prune and destroy infected lower foliage to reduce splash dispersal from soil.
Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR) Tomato Disease Advisory
FAO Integrated Pest Management Guidelines for Solanaceous Crops

symptoms: Irregular dark water-soaked lesions on leaves rapidly turning purplish-brown
White fungal downy sporulation on lower leaf surface under humid conditions
Dark brown necrotic lesions on petioles and stems leading to rapid collapse

treatment.organic: Preventative Copper oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L) spray prior to high-humidity cool spells.
treatment.conventional: Systemic fungicide: Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb.
treatment.dosage: 500-600 liters spray volume per acre ensuring complete canopy coverage.
treatment.timing: Immediately upon first symptom detection or forecast of cool, humid overcast days.

precautions: Ensure wide row spacing to maximize canopy ventilation and rapid foliage drying.
Immediately rogue and bury heavily infected plants away from water sources.
Destroy volunteer tomato and potato cull piles in surrounding fields.
sources: ICAR Central Potato & Tomato Research Protocols

symptoms: Uniform deep green leaf pigmentation without chlorosis or necrosis
Smooth, intact foliage margins with active photosynthetic turgor
Absence of fungal sporulation, viral mottling, or insect puncture marks

treatment.organic: Maintain balanced organic soil nutrition, compost tea, and beneficial rhizosphere biology.
treatment.conventional: Standard balanced NPK fertigation schedule based on soil test calibration.
treatment.dosage: As per standard agronomic schedule for current crop growth stage.
treatment.timing: Regular scheduled irrigation and fertigation cycles.

precautions: Continue regular diagonal field scouting twice a week.
Maintain drip irrigation lines to avoid wetting foliage.

symptoms: Small dark brown to black spots on lower leaves with concentric rings
Senescence and premature dropping of heavily infected foliage
Stunting of vegetative growth when canopy defoliation occurs

treatment.organic: Neem oil emulsion (5ml/L) or Copper-based bio-fungicide foliar application.
treatment.conventional: Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L) or Propineb 70% WP (2g/L) foliar spray.
treatment.timing: Apply at first appearance of lesions; repeat at 10-14 day intervals if weather remains favorable.

precautions: Maintain adequate plant nitrogen levels to reduce stress-induced susceptibility.
Avoid overhead irrigation in late afternoon to minimize night leaf wetness.
sources: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) Disease Guide

symptoms: Water-soaked grayish-green spots rapidly expanding into large brown lesions
Whitish mildew ring around margins on lower leaf surface in humid conditions
Rapid foliar blight and stem rot with distinctive foul odor

treatment.organic: Bordeaux mixture (1%) or Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L) preventative sprays.
treatment.dosage: 500 liters per acre with high-pressure mist sprayer.
treatment.timing: Spray immediately when temperature ranges between 10-20°C with relative humidity >80%.

precautions: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers.
Kill potato haulms 10-14 days before harvest to prevent tuber infection.

symptoms: Vigorous dark green compound leaves with firm cellular turgor
No water-soaked spots, concentric lesions, or viral mottling
Healthy root and stolon development without tuber rot

treatment.organic: Maintain healthy soil organic matter and beneficial mycorrhizal inoculation.
treatment.conventional: Balanced potassium and phosphorus fertilization according to soil health card.

precautions: Monitor weather forecasts for sudden high-humidity or continuous rain periods.
Scout lower leaves along field borders and shaded rows regularly.
sources: Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Tuber Crops

symptoms: Angular water-soaked lesions strictly delimited by small leaf veinlets
Lesions turning reddish-brown to dark brown on upper leaf surface
Bacterial ooze droplets visible on underside of young lesions in morning dew

treatment.organic: Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (2.5g/L) + Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-agent.
treatment.conventional: Streptocycline (1g in 10L water) combined with Copper Oxychloride 50 WP (25g in 10L water).
treatment.timing: Apply at early squaring stage upon detecting angular foliar spots.

precautions: Use acid-delinted and certified pathogen-free seeds.
Avoid excess nitrogenous fertilization which promotes succulent susceptible tissue.
Do not cultivate or walk through wet fields to prevent bacterial dispersal.
sources: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Disease Compendium

symptoms: Small, powdery cinnamon-brown pustules (uredinia) scattered on both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupturing leaf epidermis and releasing rust-colored spores
Chlorosis and premature leaf death in severe late-stage infections

treatment.organic: Foliar application of wettable sulfur (2g/L) at early pustule emergence.
treatment.conventional: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC (1ml/L) or Mancozeb 75% WP (2.5g/L).
treatment.dosage: 400 liters per acre with fine droplet hollow cone nozzle.
treatment.timing: Apply at first sign of pustules prior to tasseling stage.

precautions: Select rust-resistant or tolerant corn hybrids.
Plant early in the season to avoid late-season spore showers.
Ensure balanced soil potassium levels to improve fungal resistance.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Protection Guidelines

symptoms: Bright yellow to orange-yellow pustules arranged in narrow parallel linear stripes along leaf blade
Powdery yellow spores rubbing off onto fingers when touched
Severe drying and yellowing of flag leaves compromising grain filling

treatment.organic: Prophylactic bio-fungicide spray of Bacillus subtilis or neem seed kernel extract.
treatment.conventional: Propiconazole 25% EC (1ml/L) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (1ml/L) foliar spray.
treatment.timing: Spray immediately at first detection of yellow stripes; critical to protect the flag leaf.

precautions: Plant recommended yellow rust-resistant wheat varieties (e.g., HD-3086, DBW-187).
Scout fields weekly during cool, moist winter conditions (December to February).
Avoid late sowing which exposes crop to peak rust spore loads.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR) Rust Advisory

symptoms: Uniform green linear blades with clean parallel venation
Absence of yellow stripes, brown pustules, or powdery mildew patches
Erect leaf posture and strong tiller development

treatment.organic: Apply organic vermicompost tea during crown root initiation.
treatment.conventional: Top dress urea/nitrogen as per recommended package of practices.
treatment.dosage: Standard fertilizer dosage based on soil test.
treatment.timing: Apply at first irrigation (CRI stage) and second irrigation (tillering).

precautions: Continue periodic field monitoring throughout the tillering and heading stages.
Maintain proper irrigation intervals without waterlogging.
